For Idan

The Summer Plan for Idan.

Spent some time sitting with where your business is at - the history of it, the recent numbers, and the stuff you sent over.

Before we talk about working together on anything bigger, I want to lay out how I'm seeing it, and then what I think the smart next move is. Mostly just facts and then a plan.

The climb

The way I think about it, a business like yours climbs in levels. And I mean profit here, not revenue. A thousand a month in profit, then ten, then thirty, then a hundred, and so on. The thing that gets you stuck is different at every level.

To get to that first thousand, the whole game is just doing it - getting volume up, getting reps in. You've cleared that. Same with the next one. You can fire, and you can fire a lot, which honestly is the part most people never get past.

You're sitting around the $30k profit mark now, which is the average of your best two months. And going from this level to the next one usually isn't about doing more. It's taking what you're already doing and doing it a little better. Better in the right places. Which is exactly the copywriter and marketer hat you've been talking about putting on - getting the messaging to punch harder for the same amount of effort.

More and better

So it's not more, and it's not better instead of more. It's more and better at the same time.

More on its own keeps running but never quite arrives. More plus better aim is what actually moves you up to the next level.

Front end, not back end

One thing I want to flag before anything else, because I think it's where a lot of people your size spend energy in the wrong place.

The instinct at this point is usually to go work on the back end - emails, upsells, SMS, squeezing more out of each customer. And that stuff matters eventually. But right now, at your volume and your margin, it barely moves the number.

I ran it on your own figures. Around $140 a sale, roughly 9% margin after tax.

If you got a really good back end going today, you're looking at maybe a couple thousand a month extra. If instead you got your daily orders up from where they are now toward a hundred a day, same store, just more well-aimed orders, you're talking north of twenty grand a month. It's not close.

To be clear, I'm not against optimizing the back end at all. It's a timing thing, not a no. Right now the front end is the bottleneck, and the back end can only ever work on however many people make it through the front. So while that number is low, even your best back-end work adds a little. Once a lot more people are coming through, the same work is worth a lot more.

So when does the back end become worth real focus? My rough answer is once you're steady at something like 50 orders a day. Around there it starts to make sense to turn to it. Before that, the front end is the lever.

Parades and pockets

The way I'd get the front end up isn't by guessing at more ads. It's by being more deliberate about who each ad is for.

You're sitting on two big markets - men with ED, and men with PE. Both are huge and both keep refilling forever, as long as there are men there's the problem. Think of each one like a parade that never empties out.

And because it keeps refilling like that, my hunch is you probably don't need to go outside of Israel to earn a doctor's salary from home. That's one of the things we'd confirm in the plan, not assume.

You don't sell to the whole parade at once though. Inside each one there are smaller pockets - guys living the same problem in a slightly different way, wanting a slightly different result. There might be a dozen of them inside the ED parade alone.

Each pocket is sitting somewhere right now, and each one wants to get somewhere that looks a little different from the next. The whole game is being intentional about that - knowing where a pocket is, knowing where it wants to go, and building the message that speaks to exactly that. Same product, but the way you talk about it changes for each one.

You're probably already touching some of these pockets without aiming at them on purpose. The unlock is treating each one like its own little project to scale - one at a time, dialed in, then the next. That's where the next big chunk of growth is.

So here's what I'd actually do

Here's what I'm proposing, just so it's clear. Not that we jump straight into a big build. First we put together the actual plan.

I'd spend the time really understanding what's going on - your account, your store, your numbers, the market - and turn that into a written six-week plan, specific to your business, that you can just run from. Once you have it, you can execute it on your own, or we can run the six weeks together. Either way it's yours.

Roughly the kind of thing it'd work through:

  • The parade and the pockets - which slices of ED and PE to go after, and in what order.
  • How to talk to each pocket - where that group is now, where they want to get to, and the message that connects the two.
  • The funnels - both sides of it. How to get more out of the ones already working by re-aiming the messaging, and where it might be worth building new ones. Which way it goes comes out of spending real time in the data.
  • Whether staying in Israel is enough to get you where you want to go, or whether another geography is worth a look. My hunch is home is plenty for now, but we'd confirm it.
  • The fodder and seeds for big ideas and theses, plus suggestions for what they could be.
  • A six-week, week-over-week plan so you know what to work on each week.

The exact shape of it I'll figure out as I get into your numbers and the market. But that's the gist - you come out of it with a clear sense of what to build, what to say, and the order to do it in.

On the six weeks - I like that length because it's short enough to get feedback quickly and adjust, but long enough that you can actually act on it and see real results, not just set things up.

The details

This first part, the plan itself, is $500. About two weeks to put together properly, so it's ready for you to dig into when you're back.

If you decide you want to run the six weeks together and execute it as a team, the $500 you put toward the plan comes off the cost of the sprint. So it goes toward the work either way.

If you're in, just say yes in Skool and I'll get going.

— Andrew
